items.title: Section: Five Factors That Decide Whether a Killing Becomes Grave

items.zh: 復次，由五因緣，殺生成重。何等為五？一、由意樂，二、由方便，三、由無治，四、由邪執，五、由其事。若由猛利貪欲意樂所作，猛利瞋恚意樂所作，猛利愚癡意樂所作，名重殺生。與此相違，名輕殺生。若有念言：我應當作、正作、已作。心便踊躍，心生歡悅；或有自作，或復勸他，於彼所作稱揚讚歎，見同法者意便欣慶，長時思量、長時蓄積怨恨心已方有所作，無間所作、殷重所作；或於一時頓殺多類；或以堅固發業因緣而行殺害；或令恐怖無所依投，方行殺害；或於孤苦、貧窮、哀慼、悲泣等者而行殺害，如是一切，由方便故，名重殺生。
items.en: Moreover, killing becomes grave through five causes and conditions. What are the five? First, through motivation. Second, through method. Third, through the absence of antidote. Fourth, through wrong clinging. Fifth, through the object. If carried out through forceful greed, forceful hatred, or forceful delusion, it is called grave killing. Opposite to this is called light killing. If one thinks: I shall do this, am doing this, have done this, and the mind leaps with joy; whether done personally or urged upon another, praised either way; delighting upon meeting a fellow practitioner of the same deed; harboured and accumulated as resentment over a long time before finally being carried out; carried out without interruption and thoroughly; killing many kinds all at once; carried out through a firm, ongoing intention; carried out upon one left terrified with nowhere to turn; or carried out upon one already solitary, impoverished, grieving, or weeping — all of this, through method, is called grave killing.

items.title: Section: A Chicken's Struggle, and a Fellow Passenger's Wrong View

items.zh: 若唯行殺，不能日日乃至極少持一學處；或亦不能於月八日、十四、十五及半月等，受持齋戒；或亦不能於時時間惠施作福、問訊禮拜、迎送合掌和敬業等；又亦不能於時時間獲得猛利增上慚愧，悔所作惡；又不證得世間離欲，亦不證得真法現觀。如是一切，由無治故，名重殺生。若諸沙門、或婆羅門，繼邪祠祀，隨忍此見，執為正法而行殺戮。由邪執故，名重殺生。又作是心：殺羊無罪，由彼羊等為資生故，世主所化。諸如是等依止邪見而行殺害，皆邪執故，名重殺生。
items.en: If one only kills, unable to keep even a single precept even briefly, unable to observe the fasting days on the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth and at the half-month, unable at any time to give charity, cultivate merit, pay respects, or practice reverent harmony, unable at any time to feel forceful, heightened shame or remorse for what was done wrong, and neither attains worldly freedom from desire nor genuine realisation of the true dharma — all of this, through the absence of antidote, is called grave killing. Certain ascetics or brahmins, continuing wrongful sacrifice, accepting this view, holding it as correct dharma, carry out killing. Through wrong clinging, this is called grave killing. Also thinking: killing a sheep carries no fault, since such creatures exist as provisions, transformed by the lord of the world for this purpose. All such killing carried out relying on wrong view is, through wrong clinging, called grave killing.

items.title: Section: The Object Itself Decides Gravity — And Theft's Own Weighing Begins

items.zh: 若有殺害大身眾生，此由事故，名重殺生。或有殺害人或人相，或父或母，及餘尊重；或有殺害歸投委信，或諸有學、或諸菩薩、或阿羅漢、或諸獨覺；或於如來作殺害意惡心出血，如來性命不可殺故。如是一切，由其事故，名重殺生。與如上說因緣相違而殺生者，名輕殺生。復次，當說不與取等，由其事故，輕重差別。餘隨所應，如殺應知。復次，若多劫盜，名重不與取。
items.en: Killing a large-bodied being is, through the object, called grave killing. Killing a human being or a foetus already bearing the human form, a father, a mother, or another deeply respected one; killing one who has sought refuge or entrusted themselves; killing a noble learner, a bodhisattva, an arhat, or a solitary awakened one; or forming the malicious intent to kill a Tathāgata and drawing blood, since a Tathāgata's own nature makes him impossible to kill — all of this, through the object, is called grave killing. Killing under circumstances opposite to what has been described is called light killing. Moreover, the gravity of theft and the rest, through the object, shall now be explained. The rest should be understood accordingly, just as with killing. Moreover, frequent plundering is called grave theft.

items.title: Section: Stealing From the Poor, Deceiving the Trusted, and Splitting the Sangha

items.zh: 如是若劫盜妙好，劫盜委信，劫盜孤貧，劫盜佛法出家之眾；若入聚落而行劫盜，劫盜有學、或阿羅漢、或諸獨覺、或復僧祇、或佛靈廟所有財物。如是一切，由其事故，名重不與取。復次，行不應行中，若母母親委信他妻，或住禁戒、或苾芻尼、或勤策女、或復正學。如是一切，由其事故，名重欲邪行。非支行中，若於面門。由其事故，名重欲邪行。非時行中，若受齋戒，若胎圓滿、若有重病。由其事故，名重欲邪行。非處行中，若佛靈廟、若僧伽藍。由其事故，名重欲邪行。復次，若為誑惑多取他財，若妙若勝而說妄語。由事重故，名重妄語。若於委信、若父若母，廣說如前乃至佛所而說妄語。由事重故，名重妄語。或有妄語令他殺生，損失財物及與妻妾，此若成辦極重殺生、重不與取、重欲邪行。此由事重，名重妄語。或有妄語能破壞僧，於諸妄語此最尤重。
items.en: Stealing especially fine goods, stealing from one who has entrusted their confidence, stealing from the destitute, stealing from the Buddhist monastic community, plundering a village, or stealing property belonging to a noble learner, an arhat, a solitary awakened one, the monastic community, or a Buddhist shrine, is, through the object, all called grave theft. Moreover, approaching one's mother, a mother-like figure, the wife of one who has entrusted their confidence, one observing the precepts, a nun, a novice, or a probationer, is all, through the object, called grave sexual misconduct. Engaging in the face rather than the proper part is, through the object, called grave sexual misconduct. Engaging while precepts are observed, at the completion of pregnancy, or during serious illness is, through the object, called grave sexual misconduct. Engaging within a Buddhist shrine or monastery is, through the object, called grave sexual misconduct. Moreover, lying in order to deceive and take especially fine or excellent wealth from another is, through the gravity of the object, called grave false speech. Lying to one who has entrusted their confidence, to one's father or mother, or, as already explained, even to the Buddha, is, through the gravity of the object, called grave false speech. Lying in a way that causes another to commit grave killing, or the loss of great wealth and of wife and concubines, if this succeeds and brings about grave killing, grave theft, or grave sexual misconduct, is, through the gravity of the object, called grave false speech. Lying capable of splitting the monastic community apart is the gravest of all false speech.

items.zh: 復次，若於長時積習親愛而行破壞。此由事重，名重離間語。

blocks.text: Fascicle 60 continues the analysis of karma: what makes the same act grave or light, and what its results are.

Master Cháng Bǎi: a strong motive to kill, with forceful affliction, makes killing grave; killing without reflection, merely going along with bad conditions, is light. The mind to kill is hard to change in one who raises fish and ducks for sale.

One keeps no precept, cultivates no absorption, does not realise the truths. Master Cháng Bǎi: quick repentance, precepts, releasing life, merit, absorption, and best of all realising the ultimate truth can lighten the karma. Holding that killing fowl for sacrifice is proper makes it graver.

Master Cháng Bǎi: killing a person is graver than killing an ant. From the embryonic stage there is already the form of a person; killing it refers to abortion. Of the Buddha, one can only draw blood, since a Tathāgata cannot be killed.

Master Cháng Bǎi: monastic property is given by devotees of the ten directions; to steal it is a great fault. A lie that breaks the community's harmony is the gravest of all false speech. Even between spouses, some times are wrong: fast days, late pregnancy, serious illness.
"Quick repentance can lighten karma." The treatise's analysis of gravity is also an analysis of hope.

quiz.q: What are the five causes by which killing becomes grave?
options: greed, hatred, delusion, conceit, and doubt, since killing arises from root afflictions and the treatise grades it by which affliction is at work
object, perception, wish, affliction, and means and completion
defiled mind, wish, that object, the deed manifesting, and completion
motivation, method, absence of antidote, wrong clinging, and the object
quiz.why: These five grade gravity. Master Cháng Bǎi: a strong motive to kill, with such forceful affliction, makes grave killing. The object-perception-wish list in fascicle 59 defines the path itself, and the five-factor list its own-mark, so these should not be confused. The English is accurate.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi separate grave and light killing by motivation?
options: forceful affliction makes it grave; weak affliction, killing unreflectively through bad conditions, makes it light
humans are grave and animals light, motivation meaning the victim
by one's own hand is grave; through another is light
many is grave; few is light
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if the motivating greed, hatred, or delusion is not strong, and one only goes along with bad conditions and kills without reflecting, this is light killing. The object has its own category later. The English "forceful" renders 猛利 well.

quiz.q: What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give of killing through firm generating conditions?
options: killing with hard weapons, 堅固 meaning blades and staffs, weapons being graver than hands, unrelated to whether the mind can change
a mind to kill not easily changed, as with raising fish or ducks for sale
killing a strong-bodied being
killing a stubborn person
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the mind to kill is hard to change, as with raising fish and ducks for sale; killing through such firm generating conditions is very heavy karma. The English "a firm, ongoing intention" fits this reading of a settled occupation.

quiz.q: What does absence of antidote include?
options: only not confessing, confession removing all karma
not knowing killing is wrong
no precepts, fasting days, merit, shame or remorse, detachment, or realisation
not killing more beings
quiz.why: The list runs from a single precept up to realisation. Master Cháng Bǎi: one does not cultivate absorption to counter it, nor the transcendent path to realise the truths. Thus antidotes run through ethics, merit, shame, and insight. The English covers all these.

quiz.q: How can existing killing karma be lessened, and why does absence of antidote make it grave?
options: karma once made cannot lessen, antidote or no, the term only describing unwillingness to practise, since nothing changes karma
only a buddha can remove it
confession, precepts, merit, absorption, and realisation lessen it; without antidote it remains
living longer lessens it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: with active antidote, quick repentance, precepts, liberating life, merit, absorption, and best of all realisation of ultimate truth, the karma can be lessened or removed; without it, the karma stays and becomes grave. This fits the later passage on commission without increase.

quiz.q: What example is given of killing grave through wrong clinging?
options: mistakenly killing kin, wrong clinging meaning misidentifying the target
killing for revenge
killing for food
continuing wrongful sacrifice as Dharma; holding sheep made by the lord of the world, killing them faultless
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: holding that killing fowl for sacrifice is proper and taking it as true Dharma; and thinking poultry exist for people to eat, killing as a matter of course. This is wrong view, and it makes killing heavy. The English "lord of the world" for 世主 is good.

options: only arhats and the Buddha's blood, as only heinous deeds count, parents and large beings being light
only humans
all beings equally
large beings, humans, parents, the trusting, noble ones, and drawing a Tathāgata's blood
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: killing a person is surely graver than killing an ant, a person being large-bodied; the traits of the object make the karma grave. The English lists these faithfully, apart from the two points taken up in the next two questions.

quiz.q: The English has "one bearing the human form." What might readers misread, and how does the lecture explain it?
options: 人相 means non-humans looking human, such as yakṣas, so that the English is right
a Buddha image
人相 means one in the womb with human shape, killing it being abortion; the English does not show this
a painted likeness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: from the embryonic stage in the womb there is already the form of a person, called 人相, and killing it refers to abortion. "One bearing the human form" could be read as something that merely looks human. A note is needed.

quiz.q: The English has "the malicious intent to harm a Tathāgata." Why is "harm" not enough?
options: "harm" suffices: no intent to kill can exist towards the unkillable, the two words being synonyms, as the lecture shows
it should be "to praise"
it should be "to follow"
殺害意 means intent to kill, answering "impossible to kill"; "harm" loses this
quiz.why: The point is that the motive is to kill while the result can only be drawing blood, since a Tathāgata cannot be killed. "Intent to harm" weakens this, and does not connect to the English's own next clause "impossible to kill."

quiz.q: Why is frequent plundering grave theft?
options: frequent repetition habituates, and even a light offence becomes grave
the amount being large, 多 meaning value and not frequency
because of being discovered
because the goods are hard to sell
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: stealing often, through frequent habituation, makes even a light offence grave; goods also differ in value. The English "frequent plundering" matches this reading of 多.

quiz.q: What makes theft grave through the object?
options: only gold and silver, by market price, whether the owner is poor or monastic having no effect
only from one's own kin
only at night
fine goods, the trusting, the destitute, monastics, villages, noble ones, the community, and shrines
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: monastics' property is given by devotees of the ten directions, and to steal it is a great fault; the nature and value of the goods and the owner make theft grave. So ownership matters as well as worth.

quiz.q: Can a married couple commit misconduct, and why is a monastery a grave wrong place?
options: no: misconduct concerns only others' spouses, and a monastery is merely a public place, unrelated to detachment
yes: any daytime; because of images
yes: on fast days, late pregnancy, or serious illness; a monastery is for training in detachment
no; a monastery poses no issue
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: even between spouses, on fast days, when the foetus is near term, or when the other is seriously ill, this is the wrong time; a monastery exists to train in detachment, so the act is improper there. The English is accurate.

quiz.q: What is the gravest false speech, and what of lying that causes killing?
options: lying to the Buddha is gravest; a lie causing killing incurs only the killing, the lie itself staying light
splitting the community is gravest; lies accomplishing grave killing, theft, or misconduct are grave through the object
lying for wealth is gravest
all lies are equally grave
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a lie accomplishing another's grave wrong itself becomes a grave offence; a lie that breaks the community's harmony is the gravest of all false speech. Lies are weighed by what they accomplish.
